% Source: manuscript/parts/part1/ch08_examples.tex.
\begin{remark}[Harmonic functions and $\log|\mathcal O^\times|$ are not the
same sheaf]
\label{rem:ch08-harmonic-vs-log}
Write $\mathcal F_C$ for the sheaf of $\mathbf R$-vector spaces generated
by germs $\log|f|$, with $f$ invertible analytic, and $\mathcal H_C$ for
Thuillier's sheaf of harmonic germs.  Then
$\mathcal F_C\subseteq\mathcal H_C$, the quotient is supported at the
type~$2$ points, and at such a point $x$ with associated residue curve
$C_x$ one has
\[
 (\mathcal H_C/\mathcal F_C)_x
 \simeq\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R.
\]
\end{remark}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch19_cld_examples.tex.
\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$C$ be a smooth proper algebraic curve, and let $W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$
be open.  For a continuous function $u:W\to\mathbf R$,
\[
                  \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[u]\geq0
        \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                  u\text{ is Thuillier-subharmonic}.
\]
Consequently every continuous CLD-psh function on $W$ is
Thuillier-subharmonic.
\end{theorem}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch19_cld_examples.tex.
\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:ch19-continuous-zero-current-harmonic}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}, let
$h:W\to\mathbf R$ be continuous.  If
\[
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0,
\]
then $h$ is Thuillier harmonic, hence harmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff and classically pluriharmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Rabinoff.
\end{corollary}

% Source: manuscript/editorial/solver_dossiers_20260911/
% p213_residual_picard_mixed_towers_20260911/CURVE_STATEMENT.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$C$ be a smooth proper algebraic $K$-curve, and let
$W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be open.  Suppose that
$h\in C^0(W,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
\[
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0.
\]
For a type~$2$ point $x\in W$, let $C_x$ be its smooth projective residue
curve and let
\[
 \operatorname{ob}_x(h)\in
 \operatorname{Pic}^0(C_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R
\]
be the residual class of the harmonic germ of $h$ at $x$.  Then the
following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h$ is ordinary CLD-smooth near $x$ and
      $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''h=0$ there as a smooth form;
\item $\operatorname{ob}_x(h)=0$.
\end{enumerate}
At points of types $1$, $3$, and $4$, the germ of $h$ is automatically
ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch15_poincare_lelong.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:classical-psh-calculus}
Classically psh functions form a sheaf and a convex cone, are stable under
finite maxima and decreasing nets, scalar extension, and analytic pullback.
If $u$ attains a local maximum at an interior point, then $u$ is locally
constant there.  A real-valued $h$ is pluriharmonic in this theory when
both $h$ and $-h$ are classically psh.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/editorial/solver_dossiers_20260910/
% p062_proper_curve_bundle_descent_20260910/STATEMENT.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-proper-smooth-curve-bundle-descent}
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed, complete non-Archimedean field with
nontrivial absolute value, let $m\geq1$, and let $B$ be a good,
topologically separated, locally holomorphically separated, paracompact,
pure $m$-dimensional strict $K$-analytic space.  Let $D$ be a nonempty
geometrically connected smooth proper algebraic curve over $K$, and put
$F:=D^{\mathrm{an}}$.  Let $\pi:Y\to B$ be a morphism, where $Y$ is a
good, topologically separated, pure $(m+1)$-dimensional strict
$K$-analytic space.  Suppose that $B$ has an ordinary analytic open cover
by $U$'s for which there is an isomorphism over $U$
\[
                         \pi^{-1}(U)\simeq U\times_KF.
\]
If $h\in C^0(Y,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, then there is a unique
$b\in C^0(B,\mathbf R)$ such that
\[
                         h=\pi^*b,
                         \qquad
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0.
\]
Moreover, $\mathrm d'[h]=0$ implies $\mathrm d'[b]=0$.
\end{proposition}

% Source: Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, Forms on Berkovich spaces based on
% harmonic tropicalizations, Corollary 7.15 in the published version.
\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-gjr-harmonic-zero-current}
Let $Y$ be a good separated strict analytic space and let $h$ be a
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic function on $Y$.  Then the restriction of
the current $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]$ to $Y\setminus\partial Y$ is zero.
In particular, if $Y$ is boundaryless, then
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$ on $Y$.
\end{corollary}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch18_delta_forms.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:ch18-harmonic-functorial}
Let $\varphi:Y\to X$ be a morphism of good strict $K$-analytic spaces and
let $h$ be an $\mathbf R$-harmonic function on an open $U\subseteq X$.
Then $\varphi^*h=h\circ\varphi$ is $\mathbf R$-harmonic on
$\varphi^{-1}(U)$.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch13_forms.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:cld-form-pullback}
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of topologically separated analytic spaces.
There is a functorial morphism
\[
                 g^*:A_X^{p,q}\longrightarrow g_*A_Y^{p,q}
\]
commuting with wedge, $J$, $\mathrm d'$, and $\mathrm d''$.
\end{proposition}

% Book-local P06.2 mixed exact-tower transfer, 19 September 2026.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let $B_0$ be a positive-dimensional good, topologically separated,
pure strict $K$-analytic space, and let $\ell\geq1$.  Suppose that
\[
 B_\ell\xrightarrow{\pi_\ell}B_{\ell-1}
 \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_1
 \xrightarrow{\pi_1}B_0
\]
is a finite tower in which every $B_j$ is a positive-dimensional good,
topologically separated, pure strict $K$-analytic space.  At every stage
assume that exactly one of the following descriptions is specified.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial standard strict
open-polydisc bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-open-polydisc-bundle-descent}; in particular, its positive
fibre dimension and chart radii satisfy the conditions there.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial analytic projective-space
bundle as in \Cref{prop:p062-projective-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$(\mathbf P_K^{q_j})^{\mathrm{an}}$ for some $q_j\geq1$.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial smooth proper split-toric
bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-smooth-proper-split-toric-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$X_{\Sigma_j}^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a smooth proper split toric $K$-variety
$X_{\Sigma_j}$ of dimension $q_j\geq1$.
\item The field $K$ is algebraically closed, the base $B_{j-1}$ is locally
holomorphically separated and paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial
proper smooth curve bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-proper-smooth-curve-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$D_j^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a nonempty geometrically connected smooth proper
algebraic $K$-curve $D_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Put $\Pi=\pi_1\circ\cdots\circ\pi_\ell$.  If
$h\in C^0(B_\ell,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, then there is a unique
$b\in C^0(B_0,\mathbf R)$ such that
\[
                  h=\Pi^*b,
                  \qquad \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0.
\]
The following properties transfer from $B_0$ to $B_\ell$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If every continuous zero-current function on $B_0$ is classically
pluriharmonic, then every such function on $B_\ell$ is classically
pluriharmonic.
\item If every continuous zero-current function on $B_0$ is
$\mathbf R$-harmonic, then every such function on $B_\ell$ is
$\mathbf R$-harmonic, hence locally $\mathbf R$-PL and
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.
\item If every $u\in C^0(B_0,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
\[
             \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[u]=0,
             \qquad \mathrm d'[u]=0
\]
is locally constant, then the same implication holds with $B_\ell$ in
place of $B_0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

% Book-local P21.3 stage-local annular rigidity package, 20 September 2026.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-stage-local-polyannulus-smooth-rigidity-transfer}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute value,
let $m\geq1$, and let $B$ be a good, topologically separated,
boundaryless, pure $m$-dimensional strict $K$-analytic space.  Let
$\pi:Y\to B$ be a morphism, where $Y$ is a good, topologically separated,
boundaryless, pure strict $K$-analytic space.  Suppose that $B$ has an
analytic open cover $\mathcal U$ such that, for every $U\in\mathcal U$,
the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is an integer $s_U\geq1$, together with radii
\[
 0<r_{U,i}<R_{U,i},\qquad r_{U,i},R_{U,i}\in|K^\times|
 \quad(1\leq i\leq s_U),
\]
and an isomorphism over $U$
\[
 \pi^{-1}(U)\simeq
 U\times_K\prod_{i=1}^{s_U}
 \{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
                  r_{U,i}<|T_{U,i}(z)|<R_{U,i}\}.
\]
\item Every $b\in C^0(U,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0$ is classically pluriharmonic and ordinary
CLD-smooth, with $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''b=0$ as a smooth form.
\item Every $b\in C^0(U,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
\[
             \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0,
             \qquad \mathrm d'[b]=0
\]
is locally constant.
\end{enumerate}
Then every $h\in C^0(Y,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$ is classically pluriharmonic and ordinary
CLD-smooth, with $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''h=0$ as a smooth form.  Moreover,
every such $h$ with $\mathrm d'[h]=0$ is locally constant.  No compatibility
among the displayed annular coordinates and no global logarithmic
coefficient formula are asserted.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower}
Let $K,C,W$ be as in
\Cref{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve}, and assume
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-vanishing}.  Let $\ell\geq1$, and suppose
that
\[
 B_\ell\xrightarrow{\pi_\ell}B_{\ell-1}
 \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_1
 \xrightarrow{\pi_1}B_0=W
\]
is a finite tower in which every $B_j$ is a positive-dimensional good,
topologically separated, boundaryless, pure strict $K$-analytic space.
At every stage assume that exactly one of the following descriptions is
specified.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is one of the four exact bundle types appearing
in \Cref{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer}, with all hypotheses
of the corresponding source proposition retained.
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is an analytically locally trivial finite
standard strict open-polyannulus bundle, and there is a trivializing
analytic open cover $\mathcal U_j$ of $B_{j-1}$ such that every
$U\in\mathcal U_j$ satisfies conditions \textup{(2)} and \textup{(3)} of
\Cref{prop:p062-stage-local-polyannulus-smooth-rigidity-transfer}.
\end{enumerate}
Then every $h\in C^0(B_\ell,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$ is classically pluriharmonic and ordinary
CLD-smooth, with $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''h=0$ as a smooth form.  Moreover,
every such $h$ with $\mathrm d'[h]=0$ is locally constant.

The stage-local hypotheses on the members of $\mathcal U_j$ are not
claimed to follow merely from the corresponding whole-space conclusions
on $B_{j-1}$.  In particular, the theorem does not assert the result for
an arbitrary locally trivial annular stage over an arbitrary intermediate
base open.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-bt}
In the setting of
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower}, assume that
$B=B_\ell$ has pure dimension $n\geq2$.  Let $T$ be a positive
$\mathrm d'$- and $\mathrm d''$-closed ordinary CLD current of bidegree
$(p,p)$, $0\leq p\leq n-1$, and let $u,v\in C^0(B,\mathbf R)$ satisfy
\[
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[u]
                         =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[v].
\]
Then
\[
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''(uT)
                         =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''(vT).
\]
In particular, this holds for every continuous psh pair in the
continuous-potential predicate of P21.3.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-cover-bt}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$X$ be a good, topologically separated, pure, boundaryless strict
$K$-analytic space of dimension $n\geq2$, and let $V\subseteq X$ be
ordinary open.  Suppose that $V$ has an ordinary open cover by sets $B$
which, with their induced analytic structures, satisfy the geometric
hypotheses of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-bt}.  Then every
positive closed ordinary CLD current $T$ of bidegree $(p,p)$ on $V$,
$0\leq p\leq n-1$, has Bedford--Taylor independence for every continuous
psh pair $u,v$ on $V$ with equal Hessian currents.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-basis-bt}
Let $K$ and $X$ be as in
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-cover-bt}.
Suppose that the ordinary topology of $X$ has a basis of open sets $B$ such
that every $B$, with its induced analytic structure, satisfies the
geometric hypotheses of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-bt}.  Then the
continuous-pair Bedford--Taylor predicate in P21.3 holds on every ordinary
open subset of $X$ for every positive closed ordinary CLD current.
\end{corollary}

% Book-local P21.3 open-nonheredity package, 20 September 2026.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p213-zero-current-smoothness-not-open-hereditary}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, and let
$D$ be a geometrically connected smooth proper algebraic $K$-curve.  Suppose
that $x\in D^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a type~$2$ point such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p213-nonhereditary-residual-class}
 \operatorname{Pic}^0(D_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R\ne0.
\end{equation}
Put
\[
 P=(\mathbf P^1_K)^{\mathrm{an}},
 \qquad X=P\times_KD^{\mathrm{an}}.
\]
Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every $H\in C^0(X,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[H]=0$ is constant.  In particular, every such
function is classically pluriharmonic and ordinary CLD-smooth with zero
smooth Hessian, and adding $\mathrm d'[H]=0$ forces local constancy.
\item There are an ordinary open neighbourhood $U\subset D^{\mathrm{an}}$
of $x$ and a function $g\in C^0(U,\mathbf R)$ such that
\[
                     \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[g]=0
\]
but $g$ is not ordinary CLD-smooth near $x$.  For
\[
 \Omega=P\times_KU,
 \qquad G=\operatorname{pr}_U^*g,
\]
one has $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[G]=0$, whereas $G$ is not ordinary
CLD-smooth near $(p,x)$ for any $p\in P(K)$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, whole-space ordinary smooth zero-current regularity is not
inherited by arbitrary ordinary open subsets, even on a smooth proper
surface which is a trivial proper smooth curve bundle over a
residual-Picard base.  Thus the stage-local chart hypotheses in
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower} cannot be removed
by invoking only the corresponding whole-space conclusions on an exact
intermediate base.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-good-reduction-elliptic-open-nonheredity}
The situation in
\Cref{prop:p213-zero-current-smoothness-not-open-hereditary} occurs.  One
may take
\[
                K=\widehat{\overline{\mathbf C((t))}}
\]
with its $t$-adic absolute value and let $D$ be the base change to $K$ of
an elliptic curve $E$ over $\mathbf C$.  At the type~$2$ point $x$
defined by the good-reduction component, one has $D_x\simeq E$ and
\[
 \operatorname{Pic}^0(D_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R\ne0.
\]
\end{corollary}
proof:
\begin{proof}[of
\Cref{prop:p213-zero-current-smoothness-not-open-hereditary}]
Let $\pi:X\to P$ be the first projection.  It is a globally trivial
proper smooth curve bundle with fibre $D^{\mathrm{an}}$.  Hence
\Cref{prop:p062-proper-smooth-curve-bundle-descent} writes every continuous
zero-current function on $X$ uniquely as
\[
                              H=\pi^*b,
 \qquad b\in C^0(P,\mathbf R),
 \qquad \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0.
\]
By \Cref{cor:ch19-continuous-zero-current-harmonic}, the function $b$ is
classically pluriharmonic.  It attains a maximum because $P$ is compact.
The local maximum assertion in \Cref{prop:classical-psh-calculus} makes the
maximum locus open; it is also nonempty and closed.  Since $P$ is connected,
$b$, and therefore $H$, is constant.  This proves the first assertion.

Write $\mathcal H_D$ for the sheaf of Thuillier harmonic germs and
$\mathcal F_D$ for the real vector subsheaf generated by germs $\log|f|$
with $f$ an invertible analytic function.  By
\Cref{rem:ch08-harmonic-vs-log},
\[
       (\mathcal H_D/\mathcal F_D)_x
       \simeq\operatorname{Pic}^0(D_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R.
\]
Choose a nonzero class using
\eqref{eq:p213-nonhereditary-residual-class}, and represent it by a
Thuillier harmonic function $g$ on an ordinary open neighbourhood $U$ of
$x$.  Both $g$ and $-g$ are Thuillier-subharmonic.  The equivalence in
\Cref{thm:wanner-curve-comparison} therefore gives
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[g]=0$.  The residual Picard criterion
\Cref{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve} shows that $g$ is not
ordinary CLD-smooth near $x$.  Moreover,
\Cref{cor:ch19-continuous-zero-current-harmonic} makes $g$ harmonic in the
sense of Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff.

Let $q:\Omega=P\times_KU\to U$ be the second projection.  Harmonic
functoriality \Cref{prop:ch18-harmonic-functorial} makes
$G=q^*g$ harmonic.  The space $\Omega$ is good, topologically separated,
strict, and boundaryless.  Therefore
\cite[Corollary~7.15]{GJR26} gives
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[G]=0$.  Fix $p\in P(K)$ and let
\[
                         s_p:U\longrightarrow\Omega,
 \qquad z\longmapsto(p,z)
\]
be the analytic section.  If $G$ were ordinary CLD-smooth near $(p,x)$,
then functorial pullback of ordinary CLD forms in
\Cref{prop:cld-form-pullback} would make
$s_p^*G=g$ ordinary CLD-smooth near $x$, a contradiction.  This proves the
second assertion and the claimed failure of open inheritance.  Finally,
every type~$2$ residue curve of $P$ is rational, so $P$ satisfies the
residual-Picard condition.  The projection $X\to P$ is a locally trivial
proper smooth curve bundle, namely the fourth exact stage in
\Cref{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer}; it is therefore one of
the exact stages allowed in the cited tower theorem.  This proves the last
scope assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[of
\Cref{cor:p213-good-reduction-elliptic-open-nonheredity}]
The field $K$ is algebraically closed and complete, with residue field
$\mathbf C$.  The constant smooth proper model of $D$ has special fibre
$E$.  Its generic point defines a type~$2$ analytic point $x$, and the
associated smooth projective residue curve is $D_x\simeq E$.  The group
$E(\mathbf C)\simeq\operatorname{Pic}^0(E)$ contains a point of infinite
order: its torsion subgroup is countable, whereas $E(\mathbf C)$ is
uncountable.  Such a point remains nonzero after tensoring with
$\mathbf R$, so \eqref{eq:p213-nonhereditary-residual-class} holds.  Apply
\Cref{prop:p213-zero-current-smoothness-not-open-hereditary}.
\end{proof}
